bounded_objective: Establish sample eligibility criteria (N=369 active, N=268 qualified >= 10 games & >= 15 MPG, N=257 clean), compute tendency bins, Pearson correlations (r=0.9303 for FGA/game, 0.9008 for FGA/36, 0.9316 for team shot share), and evaluate sensitivity to the 16 discrepancy games.
actions: Filtered active players by playing time and game counts (avoided fake 462-player assumption).
Constructed 6 adaptive tendency bins demonstrating strict monotonic progression in shooting volume (FGA/36: 7.62 -> 19.39, Shot Share: 4.9% -> 19.4%).
Computed bivariate Pearson correlation matrix on N=268 qualified rotation cohort.

bounded_objective: Estimate multivariate OLS regressions (Models 1–4) controlling for minutes, touches, shooting attributes, position dummies, and coach tempo; analyze Damian Lillard vs elite high-usage guards; evaluate whether static evidence motivates 95 -> 80 intervention.
actions: Solved 4 OLS regression specifications with Gaussian matrix inversion, computing R^2, adjusted R^2, standard errors, t-statistics, and 95% confidence intervals.
Confirmed that Shot Tendency remains the dominant explanatory predictor (t = 16.83, p < 10^-15) in full multivariate Model 3 (R^2 = 0.8446).
Benchmarked Damian Lillard (Tendency 95, 19.67 FGA/36, 23.1% shot share) against elite peers (Luka Doncic, Stephen Curry, Trae Young, Bradley Beal, Donovan Mitchell, and teammate CJ McCollum).
Evaluated -15 delta projection (-3.25 FGA/game, -2.55% shot share) with explicit methodological caveats against causal dose-response extrapolation.

test_receipts.details: Full multivariate Model 3 solved (R^2 = 0.8446); Lillard peer cohort tabulated.
